gmail.name: Gmail
gmail.step1: Turn on 2-Step Verification in your Google Account.
gmail.step2: Create an app password and copy it: Google only shows its 16 letters once.
gmail.step3: Optional: create a label (e.g. “Job alerts”) and a filter that sends emails from LinkedIn, InfoJobs, Indeed… there. Type that name in “Folder”.
gmail.step4: It doesn't work with work or school accounts, or with Advanced Protection: Google doesn't offer app passwords there.

outlook.name: Outlook / Hotmail
outlook.intro: Microsoft no longer allows IMAP sign-in with a password for work or school accounts, and has announced it will remove it for personal ones too (Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live). The app doesn't use Microsoft sign-in, so there are two ways that work:
outlook.forwardTitle: Forward the alerts to another account (recommended)
outlook.forwardBody: In Outlook.com: Settings → Mail → Rules, a rule for emails from LinkedIn, InfoJobs… with “Forward to” your Gmail. Or Settings → Mail → Forwarding, to forward everything. Then add that Gmail here.
outlook.exportBody: In Outlook on the web, open an alert → ⋯ → Download: it's saved as .eml. Put them in the folder of an “Email folder” mailbox.
outlook.imapBody: It may still work for a personal account with an app password (with 2-step verification on). If it fails with “user or password”, use one of the two ways above.
outlook.linkBasicAuth: Microsoft: apps that can't connect with a password

yahoo.name: Yahoo
yahoo.step1: In your Yahoo account security, go to “External connections” and generate an app password.
yahoo.step2: Type your full address here as the user, and that password.

icloud.name: iCloud
icloud.step1: Turn on two-factor authentication for your Apple Account.
icloud.step2: At account.apple.com → Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords, generate one.
icloud.step3: User: the part before @icloud.com. If it doesn't connect, try the full address.

imap.name: Other (IMAP)
imap.step1: Look up your provider's IMAP settings in its help: server and port (almost always 993 with SSL).
imap.step2: If your provider offers app passwords, use one: not your usual password.
imap.step3: Proton Mail has no direct IMAP and its Bridge uses its own certificate, which the app doesn't accept: export the emails as .eml.

folder.name: Email folder
folder.step1: Export the alert emails as .eml (or one .mbox) from your email program.
folder.step2: Put them in this mailbox's folder: the app reads them without moving or deleting them.
folder.step3: Works with any provider, Outlook and Proton included.

errors.imap_auth: Check the user (the full address) and that the password is an app password, not your usual one.
